How to Use the Password Generator

A new password is ready when the page opens. Change the length (8 to 64 characters) or the types of characters and it makes a fresh one straight away. Tap Copy and paste it into your password manager or the sign-up form. Hide covers it with dots if someone's nearby; Copy still copies the real password.

Private by design

The password is made on your device with Web Crypto, the browser's built-in secure random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues), never the predictable Math.random. It's never saved, sent to a server or logged. There's no account and no history. Once you leave the page, it's gone, so copy it first.

Each type you turn on appears at least once, so sites that ask for "a number and a symbol" accept it. The symbols are ones most sites allow; quotes, spaces and slashes that forms often reject are left out.

What the strength number means

The bits are length × log₂ of how many characters it can choose from. 16 characters with all four types comes to about 103 bits. Each extra bit doubles the number of guesses someone would need, so a 16-character password takes vastly longer to guess than an 8-character one. Under 60 bits is marked Weak, 60 to 89 Good, and 90 or more Strong. It's an estimate, not a promise; no tool can tell you an exact time to crack.

Ways to use it

  • A new account. One unique password per site, kept in a password manager.
  • Wi-Fi. Turn on Leave out look-alikes so guests can type it from a card without mixing up 0 and O.
  • A shared family password. Something nobody will guess but you can still read out loud.
  • Replacing a reused password. If one password guards several accounts, swap each for its own.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it really random?

Yes. Every character comes from your browser's secure random number generator (Web Crypto), the same kind used for encryption. It's not Math.random, which is predictable.

Is my password saved anywhere?

No. It's made on your device and never saved, sent or logged, so copy it before you leave. There's no way to get it back afterwards.

What length should I use?

16 characters with all four types is a strong default for most accounts. Go to 20 or more for important ones like email and banking, and use a password manager so you don't have to remember them.

What are look-alike characters?

Characters that are easy to mix up when reading or typing: lowercase l, the number 1, capital I, capital O and zero. Leave them out when someone will type the password by hand.

Can I use symbols?

Yes, they're on by default. A few sites don't accept symbols. If a site rejects the password, turn symbols off and generate another.
